subject: Rivet Systems connector: technical validation & reference design
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sasha Levin <sasha@rivetsys.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, Jun 30, 2026 at 09:12 AM -0700
Subject: Technical validation plan for Rivet connector (proposal)

Hi Sasha —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Per our conversation, we want to validate the "Rivet Connector v1.2" against Redwood Private to make sure the adapter, KV cache interactions, and batching semantics behave as expected in a production reference design. I attached a short proposal and a reference diagram.

Proposed validation scope (high level):
- Compatibility smoke: API surface, auth (mTLS + API key), and payload schemas.
- Performance smoke: 95th pct latency and token throughput at 1–2K concurrent requests.
- Behavioral tests: KV/prefix cache correctness with streaming responses and function/tool calling flows.
- Failover: adapter retry semantics and graceful fallback to a lightweight model variant.

Can your eng team share the connector spec and the logs from a recent test run? I'm CC'ing Laura and Vivek to propose owners for the test harness and reference deployment.

Next steps:
1) Rivet shares connector spec and a quick-run smoke test output (today/tomorrow).
2) Redwood spins up a Private staging stack (we'll provide a temporary VPC endpoint) and run bench harness.
3) Joint validation call to review findings and plan a canary rollout.

Thanks —
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0142

Karthik —

Appreciate the clear plan. We've attached the connector spec (rivet_connector_v1.2-spec.pdf) and a CSV of our internal smoke run (rivet-smoke-tests.csv). High-level notes:
- Auth: connector supports mTLS and token-based auth; we can instantiate a temporary client cert for the staging VPC.
- Batching: the connector batches up to 32 requests by default; configurable.
- KV semantics: per-session KV with TTL; caching sits in-process in the adapter but can be externalized to Redis.

We'll stand up a team to run the joint validation. Tom (cc'd) will be our partner eng lead. Available to join a call Thu (7/1) morning PT.

—Sasha

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, Jun 30, 2026 at 02:20 PM -0700
Subject: Re: Technical validation plan for Rivet connector (proposal)

Quick read of the spec: several items we should explicitly test beyond the proposed list — I noted inline questions in the spec but calling these out here: 
- Tokenization alignment: ensure Rivet's pre-tokenization and Redwood's tokenizer are consistent for chunking/streaming. Mismatch will break prefix cache hits.
- Batching semantics: when Rivet batches, do we preserve request ordering and per-request stop conditions? We need deterministic per-request termination for streaming.
- KV eviction: confirm TTL behavior under high load; surface a metric for per-session cache misses.
- Fallback path: define a clear contract for fallback to a smaller model (e.g., quantized variant) including response format parity.

I'll volunteer to own the bench harness (we use benchr/benchr-runner internally). If Rivet can provide a containerized adapter image and sample payloads, we can run all tests in our staging VPC.

-Vivek
Sr. Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
Vivek Kulkarni | vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai

Karthik / Vivek —

Thanks — we'll get the container image pushed to a temporary GCR repo by EOD and attach the sample payloads. A few clarifications from our side:
- Batching ordering: default behavior preserves enqueue order; we can expose a "disable_batching" flag for deterministic single-request behavior.
- Tokenizer: Rivet uses a UTF-8 pre-tokenizer that is byte-level compatible with standard GPT-style tokenizers; we'll include a small verification script.
- KV eviction: current default TTL is 10m; we can add metrics for misses and eviction counts.

We can confirm Thu 7/1 10:00 AM PT for a short run. Will upload artifacts to the Drive folder and share links.

Cheers,
Tom Nguyen

Subject: Re: Rivet Systems connector: test run summary & canary plan

Team —

Summary after today's run and next steps for a canary:

Observations:
- Connector image booted in our staging VPC and passed auth using the temporary client cert.
- Benchr-runner results: no tokenizer mismatches in 500 sample sessions; 95th pct latency when batching at 16 was 180ms (within our target).
- KV TTL behavior caused a small spike in cache misses under synthetic churn; Vivek's team collected eviction metrics (see Drive logs).

Action items / owners:
- Rivet (Tom): expose "disable_batching" toggle and include the tokenizer verification script in the repo (due 7/6).
- Redwood Eng (Vivek): add eviction-count metric to the reference diagram and update alerting thresholds (due 7/5).
- Redwood AM (Karthik/Laura): draft a one-page reference design and canary checklist for the SOW addendum (Karthik to draft by 7/7; Laura to review).

Canary plan (brief):
1) Deploy connector to a single Dedicated node pool (10% traffic) with monitoring and a rollback policy.
2) Run two prompt regression suites (functional + hallucination checks) against canary traffic.
3) If stable for 48 hours, increase to 40% and begin revenue traffic ingress.

I'll prepare the one-pager and the canary checklist; Karthik, please coordinate commercial language with Rivet's partnership team.

Thanks —
Laura Bennett
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
